solves.reasoning: (A) perception fits 'the ___ of difference', (B) detect fits 'not be able to ___ a 1-mm difference', (C) comparing fits 'we are ___ a line'
(A) notice fits 'may not ___ the light', (B) varies fits 'JND ___', (C) strength fits '___ of the signals'
(A) greater fits 'JND is ___ for loud noises', (B) barely fits 'even if it is ___ louder', (C) distinguish fits 'harder to ___ between two samples'
② overlook(간과) replaces detect(감지). Context: 'able to overlook a difference' contradicts the intended meaning of detecting.
④ smaller replaces greater. Context: 'JND is smaller for loud noises' contradicts Weber's law — JND should be greater.
③ intense replaces weak. Context: 'When a sound is very intense' + 'barely louder' contradicts — if intense, barely louder wouldn't suffice.
Blank: 'not be able to ___ a 1-mm difference'. detect fits. 'we may be able to detect' appears later confirming.
Blank: 'may not ___ the light from this candle'. notice fits the perception context.
Blank: 'harder to ___ between two samples'. distinguish fits with 'between'.
perception = recognition (both mean awareness/sensing of something)
distinguish = differentiate (both mean to tell apart)
varies = fluctuates (both mean changes/differs)
weak ↔ powerful (opposite in intensity)
harder ↔ simpler (opposite in difficulty)
(A) function = 함수/mathematical relationship ('as a function of'), (B) function = 기능하다/work ('expected to function independently')
'something that causes a physical reaction' = stimulus
bare → barely: adverb needed to modify 'louder'
perceive → perception: noun needed after 'the'
JND varies as a function of signal strength — matches the examples about loud/quiet sounds
Weber's law = larger/stronger stimuli make distinction harder — this is the conclusion of the passage
